method: Opened/read primary-text PDF extraction and Newton Project normalized primary text via web tool. No UI/browser playtest.

sources.locator: Book III, Proposition IV and scholium; printed pages 391–393; PDF zero-based pages 8–10
sources.verified: The passage compares lunar deflection and terrestrial fall using a roughly sixty-Earth-radius lunar distance and squared-distance scaling. It discusses the fixed-Earth approximation and a correction when Earth and Moon move.
sources.adaptation: 4.90 m, a 27.3-day period, a 6.37-million-metre Earth radius, and the same-one-second 1.36 mm comparison are supplied rounded modern-unit teaching quantities, not historical measurement quotations. The circular formula is explicitly a short-time model.

sources.locator: General Scholium; normalized 1729 English text; printed page 392, paragraphs beginning Hitherto and But hitherto
sources.verified: Newton distinguishes a gravitational account of phenomena from having established gravity’s cause. The opening of the scholium also disputes vortex explanations, but this candidate does not pretend to have numerically tested one.
sources.adaptation: The exercise keeps cause open without erasing Newton’s own theological discussion or claiming the later Scholium was an available 1687 object.

mathematicalChecks.roundingConclusion: Both values round to 1.36 mm, but they are not numerically identical before rounding.
mathematicalChecks.accelerationRelation: a ≈ 2d/(Δt)²; surface a ≈ 9.80 m/s², lunar a ≈ 0.00272 m/s².
